definitions.explanation: The size and depth of a person's vocabulary, especially in the context of language learning or communication skills.

examples.japanese: {単語力|たんごりょく}をつけるには{毎日|まいにち}の{積|つ}み{重|かさ}ねが{大切|たいせつ}だ。
{読解|どっかい}の{成績|せいせき}は{単語力|たんごりょく}に{左右|さゆう}されることが{多|おお}い。
examples.english: Reading comprehension scores are often influenced by vocabulary ability.

examples.japanese: {英語|えいご}の{単語力|たんごりょく}を{伸|の}ばすために、{毎日|まいにち}{新|あたら}しい{単語|たんご}を{十個|じゅっこ}ずつ{覚|おぼ}えるようにしている。
examples.english: To improve my English vocabulary, I try to learn ten new words every day.

notes:
A compound of {単語|たんご} (word, vocabulary) and {力|りょく} (power, ability). Commonly used in language learning and test preparation contexts. The {〜力|りょく} suffix is productive in Japanese, forming many ability-related compounds.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {単語力|たんごりょく}をつける: to build vocabulary
- {単語力|たんごりょく}を{伸|の}ばす: to expand vocabulary
- {単語力|たんごりょく}が{足|た}りない: to lack vocabulary
- {単語力|たんごりょく}テスト: vocabulary test

RELATED WORDS:
- {語彙力|ごいりょく}: vocabulary ability — a more formal synonym; {語彙|ごい} is the academic term for vocabulary while {単語|たんご} is more casual
- {読解力|どっかいりょく}: reading comprehension ability — another {〜力|りょく} compound for a language skill
- {表現力|ひょうげんりょく}: expressive ability — the skill of putting thoughts into words
